## Task
Improve the post-route quality of `addpipe32` (32-bit registered adder: y = a + b (mod 2^32)) without changing its behavior.

## Specification (current RTL, also the equivalence reference)
```verilog
module addpipe32 (
    input  wire        clk,
    input  wire        rst_n,
    input  wire        valid_i,
    input  wire [31:0] a_i,
    input  wire [31:0] b_i,
    output reg         valid_o,
    output reg  [31:0] y_o
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        valid_o <= 1'b0;
        y_o     <= 32'd0;
    end else begin
        valid_o <= valid_i;

        if (valid_i)
            y_o <= a_i + b_i;
    end
end

endmodule
```
Your design must be cycle-for-cycle equivalent to this module from reset: same ports, synchronous active-low reset, `valid_o` follows `valid_i` one cycle later, and `y_o` updates only on valid cycles and holds otherwise.

## Flow and objective
Yosys/ABC synthesis to the Nangate45 library, then OpenROAD placement, clock tree synthesis and routing with a 10 ns clock and a fixed floorplan. Score = 10 * WNS_ns - 0.001 * area_um2, where WNS is the worst setup slack after routing and area is total standard-cell area. Higher is better.

This RTL measured: area 746.13 um^2, WNS 7.48722 ns, score 74.12607.
estimate_ppa on this RTL returns area 671.384 um^2, WNS 7.57073 ns, estimated score 75.035916 (estimates omit tap cells, buffering and wiring, so compare estimates with estimates).

## Rules
- One module of synthesizable Verilog-2005 (no helper modules or instances; the equivalence checker compares flat modules). The module name and ports must not change.
- No initial blocks, system tasks, compiler directives or technology cells.
- place_and_route budget: 4 submissions. Every submission counts, including failed ones.
- At most 30 tool calls in total.

Tools available: simulate, prove_equivalence, estimate_ppa, place_and_route, finish. Your score is the best verified place_and_route score. Call finish when you are done.

Actually, we could use a multiplexer at the input of the register to make sure the synthesis tool can optimize better. For example:

```verilog
module addpipe32 (
    input  wire        clk,
    input  wire        rst_n,
    input  wire        valid_i,
    input  wire [31:0] a_i,
    input  wire [31:0] b_i,
    output reg         valid_o,
    output reg  [31:0] y_o
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        valid_o <= 1'b0;
        y_o     <= 32'd0;
    end else begin
        valid_o <= valid_i;
        y_o <= valid_i ? (a_i + b_i) : y_o;
    end
end

endmodule
```

This is functionally identical to the if-statement version, just expressed as a mux - synthesis tools typically treat these the same way though, so this alone probably won't move the needle much.

Reset values, combining operations, or restructuring data are all fixed by spec, so there's little room there. What might actually help is trying different synthesis directives or reorganizing assignments to nudge the tool toward a particular implementation.

I sketch a variant using a wire for y_next combined with non-blocking assignments in the always block, computing a_i + b_i conditionally based on valid_i. But this is likely equivalent to what I already have—just moving the mux into a separate wire expression rather than doing it inline.

The core logic can't really change since holding y_o when valid_i is low is essential. Before trying more variations, I should establish a baseline: simulate the original design to confirm correctness, then run estimate_ppa on a few candidates to see if any structural change actually moves the needle.

I'll test the original, then an explicit mux version (`y_o <= valid_i ? (a_i + b_i) : y_o;`), and maybe one more variant with restructured logic. Since place_and_route is limited to 4 submissions, I'll only send the most promising candidates from estimate_ppa results.
